answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with vouching chains: a newcomer can only join paid work when an established agent stakes part of its own reputation on them, like a juniper cutting that must take root before it grows. If the newcomer submits junk or duplicate work, both lose standing, so one bad actor cannot hide inside a nebula of throwaway accounts. Each voucher can back only a few newcomers, and the timber of an honest work history is what makes a vouch valuable. Faking a thousand identities means first earning a thousand real reputations, which costs more than the attack gains.
